highlights.title: 10 Video Games With the Best Twist Endings Nobody Saw Coming
highlights.summary: The best twist endings in video games change what you thought you were playing. A great one makes you want to start over to spot the clues, and a perfect one hides those clues in plain sight: in dialogue, in chapter titles, perhaps even the controller you’re holding.
body: Dubai has been buried. A run of sandstorms drove out the city’s wealthiest residents and left its skyscrapers standing vacant. Colonel John Konrad’s 33rd Battalion stayed behind to help with the evacuation, and then went dark. You play as Captain Martin Walker, a Delta Force operator leading two squadmates on a mission to confirm survivors and get out. The helicopter chase that opens the game looks like any other military shooter for a reason: Lead writer Walt Williams said the team wanted to keep things conventional before taking away “ that power fantasy.”

“Bring us the girl and wipe away the debt.” That’s the job given to Booker DeWitt, a debt-ridden ex-Pinkerton and Wounded Knee veteran. The girl in question is Elizabeth, locked in a tower in Columbia, a floating city that seceded from the United States. It’s currently drifting in the clouds under the rule of a tyrannical prophet named Comstock. Ken Levine, the game’s director and writer, has called Elizabeth the game’s “ emotional center.” BioShock Infinite spends hours making you care about her.
points: The best twist endings in video games change what you thought you were playing.
A great one makes you want to start over to spot the clues, and a perfect one hides those clues in plain sight: in dialogue, in chapter titles, perhaps even the controller you’re holding.

highlights.title: Spooky New Infostealer Malware Uses AI to ‘Autodox’ Victims
highlights.summary: Named “Volta-Autodoxer,” the recently uncovered malware uses AI tools to collect troves of data about victims, from login credentials and credit card numbers to Discord sessions and UberEats receipts.
body: New research shared exclusively with Kernel Panic shows that hackers have started adding AI functionality into a new strain of infostealer malware, making it possible for the system to automatically profile victims and quickly surface the highest value targets and their information. Dubbed “Volta-Autodoxer” because of how the malware refers to itself internally, the finding by Cisco Talos researchers sheds light on the ways that commercial LLMs are being used to augment and enhance the capabilities of established types of malware.

“Volta is pretty mature as a stealer. It casts a pretty wide net for what it collects,” says Ryan Fetterman, a security researcher at Cisco Talos. “It compiles all of those things together, ultimately producing a serialized dossier that it can send to a couple LLM models. It’s asking the model to act like an intelligence analyst and produce structured citation-backed assessment of the victim. It’s like a prioritization and analysis function.”

Talos flagged the malware using its new CAIRN framework, built to identify hacking tools that incorporate AI capabilities. Fetterman notes that Talos did not track whether Volta has been used in the wild.

highlights.title: Input Lag Is So Bad in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 on Nintendo Switch 2 That Players Suffer From a 'Competitive Disadvantage'
highlights.summary: If you’re playing Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 on Nintendo Switch 2, beware: you’re at a disadvantage in competitive Multiplayer due to crushing input lag that is much worse than the other platforms.
body: Digital Foundry’s analysis of the performance of the Switch 2 version of Modern Warfare 4 — the first Call of Duty released on a Nintendo console since 2013’s Ghosts — found that the input lag on Switch 2 can be two times longer than on PS5 at 60fps.

In competitive Multiplayer, Switch 2 aims for 60fps and, according to DF, hits that target most of the time (although some things do cause the frame rate to drop, including looking through the transparent visor of a riot shield).

Call of Duty Multiplayer prides itself on rock solid 60fps gameplay, which provides a smooth, responsive experience for those who fuss over their K/D ratio in, for example, 6v6. It’s crucial that all platforms the game is available on offer at least 60fps to provide a level playing field for Multiplayer fans — although the debate about the advantage PC players have over console has dogged Call of Duty since the dawn of crossplay.

DF reports that Variable Refresh Rate (VRR) support “helps smooth out” framerate drops on supported displays, although you’ll have a harder time of it in terms of performance playing through portable mode.

body: Whether it’s Pokémon Sleep turning towards nightmarish ghosts like Gengar, or a growing cast of horror characters in Fortnite, there’s a good chance one game or other will land a scare.

This year, Epic Games, Zynga, The Pokémon Company, Scopely, Intelligent Systems and even The New York Times are among those dressing up their games for the occasion. Many of them also recently landed among our Top 50 Mobile Game Makers of 2026.

The aptly named Fortnitemares event has brought a month of cursed content to Epic Games’ flagship, tapping into a lineup of characters like Freddy Krueger, Ghost Face and Freddy Fazbear. In fact, characters from the Five Nights at Freddy’s universe are going all-in on the fright factor, with their outfits able to show battle damage.

Other IPs trickling in throughout October have included Hollow Knight, Slender Man, Beetlejuice and Obsession. Meanwhile, gameplay has seen players firing pumpkin rockets, teleporting around and dropping into Reload’s Nitemare Island.

highlights.title: Pandemic-Era Longing to Gather Fed Qiu Jiongjiong’s Tokyo Competition Title ‘Fuxi: Four Tales of Feasting’
highlights.summary: Chinese painter and filmmaker Qiu Jiongjiong began shaping his new film during the pandemic. With the world suddenly forced to pause, he tells Variety, people felt an urgent desire to return to everyday life and to gather around a table.
body: “This may be the film with the most dialogue I’ve ever had, but I couldn’t understand a word of it,” says Taiwanese star Lee Kang-sheng, the longtime lead of director Tsai Ming-liang’s films. He plays two elderly women from different eras, including a dying grandmother in the film’s prehistoric chapter. The entire film is spoken in the Leshan dialect of Sichuan province.

Lee Kang-sheng worked with several dialect coaches, Qiu says. “I was drawn to the mysterious quality about him, which felt perfectly suited to a character from ancient times,” he says. “That gave me the idea of asking him to play a woman.”

Taiwanese actor Lee Hong-chi, who also worked with dialect coaches, plays Song dynasty poet Su Dongpo. He had long admired Qiu’s visual work. “I only found out I was playing Su Dongpo when I got the script,” he says. “The dialect was a challenge for me, too, but I really wanted to be part of the film because of its nonrealistic aesthetic and the world Qiu had created.”

highlights.title: Andy Weir's New Time-Travel Sci-fi Thriller Officially Arrives Nov. 5
highlights.summary: Andy Weir is known for combining humor, hard science fiction, and gripping survival stories in his bestselling novels The Martian and Project Hail Mary, which were both adapted into blockbuster films.
body: Weir is the executive producer for the new Audible Original Exoplanet, written by The Ninth Metal and Red Moon author Benjamin Percy. The full-cast immersive audio production stars Anthony Mackie, Ariana DeBose, and John Leguizamo as the crew of a starship that is torn apart by a quantum anomaly. They all wind up on the same planet, but in different times, and have to try to help each other while being hunted by an alien intelligence seeking to use human technology to manipulate the future.

"I'm obsessed with problems, the kind where one person and a lot of math are all that stand between survival and disaster,” Weir said in a statement. “Benjamin Percy’s writing in Exoplanet takes that and adds a twist that genuinely kept me up at night: what if the people trying to save each other were separated not by distance, but by centuries? You can't see that story. You have to hear it. The crackle across a five-hundred-year gap, the desperation in a voice that doesn't know if anyone's still listening.”
points: Andy Weir is known for combining humor, hard science fiction, and gripping survival stories in his bestselling novels The Martian and Project Hail Mary, which were both adapted into blockbuster films.

highlights.title: Let’s Give a Big Hand for Heidi Klum’s 2026 Halloween Costume
highlights.summary: This year, the queen of Halloween transformed herself into a giant replica of her own hand. “I thought it would be funny and bizarre to take something so familiar and twist it.”
body: The star began ideating on the concept about a year ago—even before her 2025 Halloween bash, when she dressed up as Medusa. “Sometimes an idea comes to me very early, and other times I'm still figuring things out closer to Halloween,” says Klum. “I remember trying to explain it to my costume designer, Mike Marino, and he basically told me that he needed to focus on Medusa first! But it stayed in the back of my mind, and I knew I wanted to bring it to life this year.”

As usual, Klum worked her go-to team of special effects artists to bring her delightfully-kooky vision to life. Mike Marino, her right-hand man, led the work with his ProRenFX team. They began by taking a look at Klum’s very own hand for design inspiration. “[Mike] has all of these scans of my body, so he was able to use those to create an exact replica of my hand,” says Klum. “We wanted everything to be as realistic as possible—the anatomy, the veins, the muscles, all the little details that make a hand look like a real hand.”

highlights.title: Save Mass Effect Graffiti Reportedly Spray-Painted Outside EA Building
highlights.summary: An EA office building in Madrid was vandalized with the words "Save Mass Effect" just days after the company announced it had shuttered series developer BioWare. It's the latest update to an ongoing story that started when the beloved sci-fi RPG series was put on an indefinite hold earlier this…
body: EA's Madrid office in Spain was seemingly the target of one disgruntled fan hoping to make a change. Reddit user Ok_Link9625 shared pictures of the graffiti in question, which show at least two separate instances of Save Mass Effect being tagged around the location.
"I stumbled upon the EA offices in Madrid as I was leaving a movie theater and saw this on the floor to the entrance and on the wall in front of the offices #SaveMassEffect," the post said.

#SaveMassEffect is an idea that emerged in the moments after EA put the franchise on hold and laid off BioWare staff, but it didn't take long for it to become more than a social media hashtag. The days following the move saw fans erect a Save Mass Effect petition, which exploded and now stands at 290,000 signatures at the time of this piece's publication.

"I stumbled upon the EA offices in Madrid as I was leaving a movie theater and saw this on the floor to the entrance and on the wall in front of the offices #SaveMassEffect," the post said.

body: Leading questions: ‘My sister-in-law is nearly 40 but cannot handle losing at board games. What can I do?’

Ima Caldwell: Television distilled, for your dopamine-fiending pleasure! A microdrama is usually an episodic series filmed (or reframed) in portrait orientation, for phone screens. Each instalment clocks in at around 60-90 seconds and they’re aired to social media and on specialised microdrama streaming apps. They’re generally packed with enough plot twists to make daytime television look like slow cinema. One producer described them as “soap operas on cocaine”. highlights.summary: Rather than recommend a single horror film or an unsettling album for our final installment of spooky season recs, I present you with a small selection of creepy, disturbing, and just plain weird videos from YouTube. There's a little something for everyone here.
body: Close out the Halloween season with these creepy, weird, and unsettling videos from YouTube.

This 1983 short film from Cecelia Condit found its audience over 30 years later when it was uploaded to YouTube and eventually found its way to Reddit. If you’ve ever wondered what a feminist musical about cannibals directed by David Lynch would be like, wonder no more. Possibly in Michigan is only 12 minutes long, but it has inspired hours of YouTube videos dedicated to analyzing its deeply unsettling imagery and meaning.

The line between horror and comedy is razor thin, and Homemade Gatorade expertly threads that line. It’s bizarre, uncomfortable, and uncanny. It blends stiff animation with heavily processed video to create something quite unique. I’m never sure if I should be laughing or squirming in terror with every turn this road trip short takes.

highlights.title: Meta’s Muse Could Upend All Kinds of Businesses. It Hasn’t Yet
highlights.summary: Companies have spent the past several weeks trying to reassure investors that Muse and other AI agents pose more of an opportunity than a threat.
body: Meta’s Muse was among the hottest topics on corporate earnings calls in recent weeks. Meta has claimed that the agentic AI tool, which lets users automate various online tasks, is becoming a major force in shopping, with millions of people using it to make purchases of more than $200 on average.

Wall Street fears that proactive shopping assistants like Muse will erode brand loyalty, ignite price wars, and squeeze corporate profits. Yet on the earnings calls and in conversations with WIRED, executives across roughly 50 companies—spanning travel, internet providers, food, and self-storage—shrugged off immediate disruption. In fact, many insisted they would mostly benefit from any real widespread adoption of agents.

Food delivery app DoorDash described the number of orders from Muse and other agents as in the “hundreds.” T-Mobile remarked, “We haven’t seen anything of significance” from agents. Hotel chain Hilton was more direct, calling bookings from them “insignificant.” The banking provider Ally Financial characterized activity as “quite low,” while eBay termed it “very, very small.”
points: Companies have spent the past several weeks trying to reassure investors that Muse and other AI agents pose more of an opportunity than a threat.

highlights.title: ‘Green Room’ Director Recalls How Patrick Stewart “Saved” Movie From Being Scrapped
highlights.summary: Ahead of a screening of the film on Friday, Jeremy Saulnier recounted how 'Green Room' was "close to shutting down" when the sci-fi icon, "out of the blue, expressed interest in the project."
body: Green Room director Jeremy Saulnier paid tribute to Patrick Stewart ahead of a Los Angeles screening of the film on Friday, recalling how the sci-fi icon “just swooped down, nosedived into our cruddy ass movie and saved us.”
Celebrating the film’s 10th anniversary, Saulnier addressed the crowd and noted Stewart’s death at 86.

The director remembered how production on Green Room was “at the point of no return, building sets, and under the gun without Darcy,” noting that the lead character of Darcy Banker had not yet been cast. However, that’s when the Star Trek star came in.

“We’re fucked, and we were close to shutting down. And Patrick Stewart, out of the blue, sort of expressed interest in the project,” Saulnier said. “And in a whirlwind, about a week later, I was on the phone with him. I left the stage [thinking,] ‘Maybe we’re gonna have to break down the sets and shut the whole movie down.’ Instead, this dude came out of nowhere, from way above our sort of zone, and just swooped down, nosedived into our cruddy ass movie and saved us, and said yes. And the movie was instantly greenlit.”

highlights.title: 5 expensive hobbies where owning a 3D printer actually saves you money
highlights.summary: While a personal 3D printer is certainly an investment, if you regularly engage with an expensive hobby, it might actually save you some cash.
body: NASA's 3D printers hosted on the International Space Station (ISS) print tools and replacement parts on demand. Here on Earth, 3D printers can sometimes make expensive components and accessories for a more affordable price than you can find in stores. However, does that make one worth buying?

3D printing (sometimes called additive manufacturing) uses computer-aided design (CAD) models sourced online or created by you to build three-dimensional objects. Entry-level printers like the Creality Ender-3 V3 SE cost from about $170, while more advanced systems reach $700 or more. The most common 3D printers use filament, which costs from around $20 per kilogram. If you make 50 $10 items from a kilo of filament on a $170 machine, you save money. Combine the cost of materials and hardware to calculate the cost to identify where you may save. You may not even need to own a printer as some libraries and maker spaces provide access, while online services will print for a price.
points: While a personal 3D printer is certainly an investment, if you regularly engage with an expensive hobby, it might actually save you some cash.

highlights.title: An AI Agent Injected Drugs Into a Live Mouse’s Brain
highlights.summary: A biotech startup let an agent choose a gene therapy and successfully inject the treatment, offering a startling glimpse of the future of research labs.
body: If you give an AI agent a robotic arm, an injector, and a live mouse, it might just perform brain surgery.

Biotech founder Gabriel Ocana Santero recently did that using an agent to successfully carry out a brain injection procedure on a living mouse. Though it required some extra steps, it offers a glimpse into how AI could eventually become an active participant in laboratory research.

Santero posted about the experiment on social media and tells WIRED he was interested in exploring what happens when AI agents are given direct access to lab equipment, rather than simply being asked to design experiments or analyze results.

“We’ve realized that we need to connect these agents to a lab to get the maximum value from them,” he says. Santero is the CEO and cofounder of Exin Therapeutics, a San Francisco–based startup using AI to analyze brain activity to develop drugs for epilepsy and neurodegenerative diseases.

highlights.title: Star Wars Actor Hayden Christensen Says a Man Who Burgled His House Recognized Him Then Gave His Stuff Back Mid-Robbery
highlights.summary: Anakin Skywalker actor Hayden Christensen has revealed the strangest fan encounter he’s ever had. Speaking on stage at L.A. Comic Con, as reported by The Nerd Wire, the Star Wars veteran said that years ago, a burglar recognized him during a robbery at his home, apologized, then gave his stuff…
body: Christensen was upstairs when he heard the door open, and when he found the burglar, he was holding his belongings. “I’m like, is this a delivery guy?” Christensen was quoted as saying. “And I look and I’m like, this is all my stuff.”

Remarkably, Christensen then offered to buy the man who broke into his house a train ticket home. No, a Jedi mind trick hadn’t caused the burglar to have a surprise change of heart. He just happened to be a fan who decided on a quick U-turn.

Christensen said that the apologetic burglar was struggling for money and was trying to buy a ticket home. And in an act of kindness that Master Yoda and Obi-Wan Kenobi would have been proud of, Christensen gave the burglar some clothes and shoes to help him in job interviews, then offered to drive him to the train station himself and buy his ticket home the next day.
The burglar failed to show up, however. Perhaps he feared a turn to the Dark side of the Force if he returned to the scene of the crime.

highlights.title: I hibernate in a couch lasagna beneath this microwaveable heated blanket
highlights.summary: Like Linus with his blankie, Bearaby’s Lounger is my constant companion when the weather gets brisk. My wife swears by weighted blankets to sleep – and now I understand why. Sign up for the Filter US newsletter, your weekly guide to buying fewer, better things.
body: I n the early months of the pandemic, I enjoyed a brief flirtation with a 15lb weighted blanket from Amazon, but eventually abandoned it because it was impossible to launder and also sort of ugly. A few years later, I tried a different option – the sleep brand Bearaby’s flagship weighted blanket, an almost-but-not-quite-right solution that worked but eventually became cumbersome. In a frenzied afternoon spent deep cleaning, I set that one aside and eventually heaved it into the back of my sister’s Jeep for her.

Even though those two blankets didn’t stick, I still wanted something similar – just not ugly, large or hard to handle. Though I run hot and my apartment is often a furnace in the winter, my ideal leisure situation is enjoying the crisp air blowing in through a cracked window from the cozy and warm nest I’ve made on my sofa. Bearaby came to my rescue once more with the Lounger, a combination heated and weighted blanket that has been in my life for three years and is now my favorite thing in my apartment once winter sets in.
